subject: Beta Regression: problems with initial values (?) causes chain to fail in creating replicated values

messages.author: 7069744c97b29f52
messages.subject: Beta Regression: problems with initial values (?) causes chain to fail in creating replicated values
parts:
I'm attempting to implement beta regression in Stan and am using the package betareg as gut check. I am using the parameterization in terms of mean and precision and my goal is to be able to regress on both the mean and precision parameters. In betareg package for example, this is implemented with the formula convention (y ~ x1 + x2 ... | z1 + z2 ...) where the x's are covariates for mean term using a logit link and z's are the covariates for the precision term using a log link.

I have coded this up in Stan along with a minimal code to simulate and fit data in both betareg and Stan: https://github.com/daltonhance/stan_beta_reg

The problem I am encountering started occurring when I tried to implement a posterior predictive check in the generated quantities block by creating replicated data. It appears that initial values for the regression coefficients are frequently causing an issue with the beta_rng() call resulting in NaN values for the y_rep. If I run multiple chains, for about half the chains I get the following error:
[37] "Error in eval(substitute(expr), envir, enclos) : "                                                                                     
[38] "  Exception thrown at line 50: beta_log: Random variable is nan, but must not be nan!"                                                 
[1] "error occurred during calling the sampler; sampling not done"

This causes that chain to fail and not return any samples. For chains that are able to run, I can confirm that they are quickly settling on appropriate values in that they match the betareg output and the simulated values. For example, to create README.md on stackoverflow it took a few tries, but I was able to successfully get MCMC draws when rstan hit upon good initial values.

I've tried playing around a bit with initialization functions but haven't hit on a solution as of yet. Any advice on minimizing this issue? Is this a bug with beta_rng?

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Beta Regression: problems with initial values (?) causes chain to fail in creating replicated values
parts:
I don't know the betareg package or what it's doing.

Which line number is causing the problem? It's a call
to either beta_lpdf(...) or ~ beta(...). The error message
is terrible now because it refers to our deprecated name
for the underling density function, beta_log.

And the problem is the first argument to beta_lpdf or the
argument before the ~ to beta(...).

The explicit exp() operations or the one implicit in
inv_logit() can lead to overflow or underflow, which can lead
to NaN values on further operations.

You can test for is_nan(x) before computing in the generated
quantities block and just set the value to not_a_number() in
those cases. If it's only an issue with inits and warmup, it's
not a problem. This is just getting caused by our functions
throwing exceptions in generated quantities that would otherwise
cause a rejection of a draw, but there's no way to reject at
the point generated quantities are being calculated. We don't
want the generated quantities to influence the model. But it'd
be nice if in the generated quantities block we just propagated
NaN instead of throwing exceptions (but that's a lot of work).

- Bob

parts:
Hey Bob,

betareg is an R package that implements MLE beta regression. I'm simply using it as a point of comparison.

The line number throwing the error is line 50. This is second call to beta_lpdf() which takes y_rep as an argument. This leads me to believe that beta_rng is returning NaN values for at least some elements of y_rep and that feeding these NaN to beta_lpdf is what causes the error.  I've confirmed this by commenting out log_lik_rep and it associated variables. Upon doing that I still get errors causing chains to fail, but those errors are of the from  "y_rep[70] is nan, but must be greater than or equal to 0; error occurred during calling the sampler; sampling not done". 

I'm only using this step as part of a posterior predictive check of the model, using the total likelihood of observed and replicated data as an omnibus assessment of fit. So I could easily comment this out for drawing from the posterior once I'm satisfied the model is performing well.

But it sounds like what I should be doing is to check whether beta_rng is returning an nan and if so have it draw another random beta value for that element of the replicated data vector?

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Beta Regression: problems with initial values (?) causes chain to fail in creating replicated values
parts:
> On Oct 20, 2016, at 11:59 AM, Dalton Hance <dalton...@gmail.com> wrote:
>
> Hey Bob,
>
> betareg is an R package that implements MLE beta regression. I'm simply using it as a point of comparison.

If so, then if the models are the same, Stan's optimize
should return the same (penalized) MLE.

> The line number throwing the error is line 50. This is second call to beta_lpdf() which takes y_rep as an argument. This leads me to believe that beta_rng is returning NaN values for at least some elements of y_rep and that feeding these NaN to beta_lpdf is what causes the error.

That's the only way that error should be able to arise on that line.
Our beta_rng shouldn't be returning NaN though. If you could trap the
inputs that cause beta_rng to return NaN that'd be super helpful. If
that's what's going on, it should be easy to fix, or at least trap on
our side with a warning message.

> I've confirmed this by commenting out log_lik_rep and it associated variables. Upon doing that I still get errors causing chains to fail, but those errors are of the from "y_rep[70] is nan, but must be greater than or equal to 0; error occurred during calling the sampler; sampling not done".

You can kill that problem by removing the constraint on y_rep. It's
only there for error checking in generated quantities.

> I'm only using this step as part of a posterior predictive check of the model, using the total likelihood of observed and replicated data as an omnibus assessment of fit. So I could easily comment this out for drawing from the posterior once I'm satisfied the model is performing well.
>
> But it sounds like what I should be doing is to check whether beta_rng is returning an nan and if so have it draw another random beta value for that element of the replicated data vector?

You can just trap this in Stan this way:

if (is_nan(y_rep[n]))
print("A[n]=", A[n], "; B[n]=", B[n]);

to see what the parameters are causing the problem.

- Bob

You can just trap this in Stan this way: 

  if (is_nan(y_rep[n])) 
     print("A[n]=", A[n], "; B[n]=", B[n]);

I'm not able to get Stan to print out the values using this. Although I still get the error caused by the beta_lpdf every couple of chains. So it will either run fine and not print out any values, meaning y_rep does not take a NaN value during the sampling, or it will crash before it gets to sampling and simply give me the "error occurred during calling the sampler, sampling not done" message.

If I take out the if statement but leave the print, I get plenty of (reasonable) A[n] and B[n] values for chains that successfully get to the sampling.

Whatever the problem is, it seems it only occurs before the sampler kicks in, not after. If that's the case, would that result in it not getting to the error trap?

I don't have another machine to test on, but I've updated the beta_regression.R on my github to include the error trap in case any body wants to dig deeper.

https://github.com/daltonhance/stan_beta_reg

Thanks for giving it a whirl. I recreated the bug and have created an issue:

https://github.com/stan-dev/math/issues/419

It arises with small values of A and B (less than or equal to 0.001). I was
able to print in generated quantities as I suggested using RStan 2.12 in the
terminal (Rstudio or the GUI behavior may be different due to buffering I/O).

We'll try to fix this for the next release. For now, you might want to
check for small A and B and do something different (like just
returning 0 or 1 with proportion A/(A + B), though those don't
work well when plugged into Bernoulli or binomial distributions).

- Bob
